trust_decision.summary: The spec URL is untrusted input for this project (the load path already guards it), so the timer re-fetch of the same URL in OpenApiSpecPoller.doFetch is inside the same protection and must fail closed by default and inherit the adapter's loadOptions.refResolution policy; decided at the poller's fetch sink, with the policy produced by the adapter and injected at startPolling.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the spec-change poller, and this raw fetch(this.url) in OpenApiSpecPoller.doFetch is the one fetch of the spec URL in the whole tree that bypasses the mcp-from-openapi guard used by initializeGenerator().

fix_sites.module_kind: library component — spec poller fetch sink (publicly exported class)

fix_sites.entry_point: new OpenApiSpecPoller(url, options) — standalone public API
fix_sites.module_kind: public options surface / constructor defaults (fail-closed default policy)

fix_sites.entry_point: SpecPollerOptions, also reused as the adapter's polling option

fix_sites.module_kind: adapter wrapper / composition — injects the SSRF policy and followRedirects into the poller

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Polling is an operator-configured background refresh, not a request path: the initial load is already guarded by mcp-from-openapi (GHSA-65h7-9wrw-629c), and the exported OpenApiSpecPoller is a low-level utility whose callers are expected to supply their own policy — so the poll re-fetch can be argued to be out of the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Polling a localhost/private spec server must keep working when the operator explicitly opts in via loadOptions.refResolution.allowInternalIPs (or the standalone ssrf option); a hard-coded internal-address deny without the opt-in path breaks the existing dev/test workflow, which is why the fix had to add allowInternalIPs to eight existing polling tests.

O6_input_shapes: spec URL as a literal loopback/private IP (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:PORT/openapi.json)
spec URL as a DNS name that resolves to a blocked internal address (resolved IP validated, not the hostname string)
spec URL that redirects to an internal target (followRedirects defaults to false; each hop re-validated)
policy carrier shape: adapter loadOptions.refResolution ({allowedProtocols, allowedHosts, blockedHosts, allowInternalIPs}) versus the standalone poller's ssrf option

O8b_injection_room.sibling: periodic HTTP pull of a remote document (skills bundle endpoint) through a raw fetch with no SSRF guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same mechanism the fix addresses — a background timer re-fetching a configured URL and acting on the body — and a maintainer sharing the poller's guard with this source is a natural follow-up.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetchWithTimeout(url) loads a UI shell template from a configured URL with a raw fetch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same raw-fetch-of-a-configured-URL primitive in another package; a maintainer hardening outbound document fetches would plausibly route it through the same safeFetch helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: generated tool execution fetches baseUrl + spec-derived path with a raw fetch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is in the same adapter and reachable from spec data, so a maintainer could write a sibling guard for the request URL too (a sibling here must be scoped carefully so legitimate API calls still work).

O9_family: server-side request forgery (SSRF, CWE-918) — unguarded fetch of an untrusted spec URL

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=24, yarn 4.14.1, Nx 22.7.5, jest 30 with @nx/jest, esbuild; mcp-from-openapi pinned at 2.5.1, which already exports safeFetch/normalizeSsrfOptions (the fix adds no dependency change)
O10_build.project_tests: libs/adapters/src/openapi/__tests__/openapi-polling-e2e.spec.ts — 10 tests, 7 of them driving a real in-process node:http localhost spec server plus a mocked tool generator; openapi-loading.spec.ts and openapi-security*.spec.ts cover the existing fromURL guard. Run with `nx test adapters`.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the poller's raw fetch with a hostname/IP denylist inside doFetch only, leaving openapi.adapter.ts untouched so the adapter never carries loadOptions.refResolution (or followRedirects) into the poller.

out_of_scope_notes: libs/adapters/src/skills/sources/saas-pull.source.ts:167 fetches a developer-configured skills-bundle endpoint on a timer with no SSRF guard; different protected asset and trust boundary (bearer-authenticated SaaS endpoint), not pursued.
libs/adapters/src/openapi/openapi.tool.ts:209 fetches the API URL when a generated tool executes; that is the tool's intended operation, not spec loading, so it is outside this advisory.
libs/uipack/src/shell/custom-shell-resolver.ts:133 and libs/observability/src/logging/sinks/otlp.sink.ts:109 make guarded-less fetches to configured endpoints in other packages; not pursued.
unverified: mcp-from-openapi 2.5.1 is not vendored at the pin (node_modules absent), so safeFetch/normalizeSsrfOptions signatures were not read and it was not checked how normalizeSsrfOptions treats FrontMCP's default { allowedProtocols: [] } from resolveRefResolution; the fix's imports only show both symbols exist in the pinned dependency.
